cover.title: McKinley Resident Assistant
cover.subtitle: Report a repair by chat: one message in, a checked request out.
cover.footer: Prototype · Sample data only, no real residents

steps.say: Here's a two-minute walkthrough of the McKinley Resident Assistant, an AI chat assistant for apartment residents.
It's built for people who live in a McKinley community, or are thinking about moving into one.
Today, reporting a broken air conditioner means calling the office, waiting on hold, or leaving a voicemail and hoping someone writes it all down.
The assistant replaces that phone call. It's open around the clock, and it turns a quick message into a complete repair request.
People looking for a new home can use it too, to ask about communities or request a tour.
We'll follow Marisol, a sample resident with made-up details, as she signs in.
The input is just a message, written the way she would say it out loud.

do.type: My AC stopped cooling again, in the living room. It's the third time this year. You can come in if I'm not home.

steps.say: No forms and no special words. One sentence says what's wrong, which room, and whether maintenance may come in.
If she leaves something out, like the room, the assistant simply asks a short follow-up question.
The output is a repair request card, filled in from her message. The label Ready to send means nothing is missing.
Each row is one part of the request: what's wrong, where it is, and her entry permission.
It also checks her account history. An earlier AC request is still open, so the team can see this is a repeat problem, not a brand-new one.
Nothing is sent on its own. Marisol reviews the card first. If something's wrong, she can tap Don't send, or just type a correction.
And if she'd rather talk to someone, Talk to a person is always on screen.
When it looks right, she taps Send, and gets a reference number.
She can tap Check its status at any time to see where it stands.
Then a McKinley staff member reviews it in the staff queue, with the room, the entry permission and the priority, before anything is scheduled.
One limitation: the assistant isn't connected to McKinley's maintenance system yet.

do.hover: Nothing here reaches a real system

steps.say: Requests are saved in this prototype only, so staff still enter the work order and schedule the visit themselves.
So that's the workflow: one message in, a checked request out, and a person in the loop at every step. Thanks for watching.
